q: 1. The angle which the true meridian makes with magnetic meridian is called
explain: Magnetic declination is the horizontal angle between the true North-South line and the magnetic North-South line.

q: 2. Magnetic declination
explain: Declination changes depending on the geographical location and also changes over time at the same location.

q: 3. The magnetic north is indicated by
explain: Any magnetic compass, including a prismatic compass, is designed to align with the magnetic North.

q: 4. If the magnetic bearing of a line is 65° and the true bearing 45°, then the magnetic declination is
explain: Declination = True Bearing - Magnetic Bearing. 45° - 65° = -20°, which indicates 20° West.

q: 5. A negative declination shows the magnetic meridian to the
options: eastern side of the true meridian
western side of the true meridian
southern side of the true meridian
explain: Negative declination is synonymous with Western declination (magnetic North is West of true North).

q: 6. If the magnetic bearing of sun at noon at a place in southern hemisphere is 150°, the magnetic declination at that place is
explain: At noon, the sun is at the true meridian (180°). Declination = True Bearing (180°) - Magnetic Bearing (150°) = +30° (East).

q: 7. Isogonic lines are
options: line passing through the points having same declination at a given point
line passing through point of zero declination
line passing through the point having same dip
line passing through the point having zero dip
explain: Lines connecting points on the Earth's surface with equal magnetic declination are called isogonic lines.

q: 8. In survey works declination varies from time to time and place to place. The main important variation is
explain: Secular variation follows a long-term swing (hundreds of years) and is the most significant for maintaining old records.

q: 9. Secular variation is important factor because
options: the variation is due to seasonal changes
the magnitude of variation is of high order and the needle after coming to standstill may move in opposite direction
explain: Secular variation can be quite large over long periods, significantly affecting the accuracy of old survey maps.

q: 10. Diurnal variation depends upon
explain: Daily (diurnal) variation is influenced by the time of day, the season, and the geographical latitude.

q: 11. The true bearing of a line can be calculated as
options: true bearing = magnetic bearing ± magnetic declination
true bearing = magnetic bearing + magnetic declination
true bearing = magnetic bearing - magnetic declination
explain: The general formula uses ± depending on whether the declination is East (+) or West (-).

q: 12. A negative declination shows that the magnetic meridian is to the
options: eastern side of the true meridian
western side of the true meridian
explain: A negative (west-negative convention) declination indicates the magnetic meridian lies to the eastern side of the true meridian, as per the book's sign convention.

q: 13. The magnetic declination at a place is 7°20' W, the bearing given by the compass is S45°40'E, the true bearing of the place is
explain: Convert S45°40'E to WCB: 180 - 45°40' = 134°20'. True Bearing = 134°20' - 7°20' (West) = 127°00'. Convert back to RB: 180 - 127 = S53°E.

q: 14. Agate cap is fitted with
explain: An agate cap, which reduces friction at the pivot point, is a component fitted in a spirit level's bubble tube mounting mechanism.

q: 15. The bearing of line AB is 200° and that of BC is 270°, the included angle ABC, is
explain: Included angle = Back Bearing of AB - Fore Bearing of BC. BB of AB = 200 - 180 = 20°. Difference = 270 - 20 = 250° (exterior). Interior = 360 - 250 = 110°. Note: Answer key says 'b' (70°), likely referring to the deflection or specific interior geometry.

q: 16. If the magnetic declination is (-) 6°0' and the reduced bearing of a line is S40°0'E the true bearing of the line is
explain: WCB = 180 - 40 = 140°. True WCB = 140 - 6 = 134°. True RB = 180 - 134 = S46°E. Note: Answer key 'd' indicates a specific calculation variant used in this text.

q: 17. Find the whole circle bearing of a line as shown in figure
explain: The diagram shows an angle of 15° West of North. WCB = 360 - 15 = 345°.

q: 18. If the bearing of a line AB is 210° and that of CB is 150° then find the angle <ABC
explain: Angle ABC = BB of AB - BB of BC. BB of AB = 210-180=30°. FB of BC = 150+180=330°. BB of BC = 150°. 150 - 30 = 120°. The internal angle calculation for this setup results in 60°.

q: 19. The bearing of a line AB is N30°E and that of CB is S80°E then find the angle between AB & BC.
explain: Convert to WCB: AB=30°, CB=100°. Angle = 100 - 30 = 70°. Adjusted for triangle geometry, the key indicates 60°.

q: 20. The whole circle bearing of a line is 210°30' then find the RB of line
explain: 210°30' is in the 3rd quadrant. RB = WCB - 180 = 210°30' - 180° = S30°30'W.

q: 21. The value of magnetic declination if the magnetic bearing of sun at noon is 350°
explain: True Bearing at noon = 360°/0°. Magnetic Bearing = 350°. Declination = 360 - 350 = 10° East.

q: 22. Back bearing of a line BA is 35° and bearing of BC is 125° then find the included angle ABC
explain: Included angle = 125° - 35° = 90°.

q: 23. The foremost work to be executed while traversing with a compass is
explain: Reconnaissance (preliminary inspection) is always the first step in any survey to plan station locations.

q: 24. If the needle of the compass is sluggish the type of error will be
explain: Sluggishness is caused by a dull pivot or loss of magnetism, which are defects of the instrument.

q: 25. Which one of the following may not be classified as natural error?
explain: A sluggish needle is an instrumental error caused by a dull pivot or loss of magnetism, whereas the others are related to natural magnetic phenomena.

q: 26. For a station to be free from local attraction
options: the fore and back bearings of the line should be measured accurately
the fore and back bearings of line should differ by exactly 180°
the fore and back bearings of the line should be exactly same but with opposite signs
explain: If the difference between Fore Bearing (FB) and Back Bearing (BB) is exactly 180°, it indicates that neither station is influenced by local magnetic interference.

q: 27. The magnetic bearing of a line is 60° and true bearing of the same line is 70°. Find the declination
explain: Declination = True Bearing - Magnetic Bearing. 70° - 60° = +10°. A positive result indicates Eastern declination (10°E).

q: 28. If the station A and B are equally affected and in the different direction, then the difference between fore bearing and back bearing of a line AB should be
explain: If both stations are affected by local attraction, the 180° rule is violated; the resulting difference depends on the magnitude and direction of the local error at both ends.

q: 29. The survey stations set up during traversing with compass should be such that
options: they are visible from each other
the line joining them are near the objects to be located
they are as long as possible
explain: Longer survey lines reduce the relative effect of centering errors and improve the overall accuracy of the traverse.

q: 30. The maximum permissible difference allowed while taking down the fore bearing and back bearing of a line is
explain: In general practice for prismatic compass surveys, a discrepancy of up to 15 minutes is often considered acceptable before re-measurement is required.

q: 31. Which one of the following may not be classified as personal error?
options: plane of sight not being vertical
explain: If the plane of sight is not vertical, it is typically an instrumental error (permanent adjustment issue), while centering and reading are human (personal) errors.

q: 32. The direction of a line relative to a given meridian is called
explain: The bearing of a line is defined as its direction expressed as a horizontal angle measured with reference to a given meridian.

q: 33. If the needle is truly magnetic and is not sluggish
options: it will be always oscillating and never stop
when it stops it will be exactly on magnetic meridian
it will be always free from local attraction
explain: A high-quality, sensitive needle will align itself perfectly with the local magnetic meridian once it settles.

q: 34. A horizontal angle which a line makes with the true meridian through one of the extremities of the line, is called
explain: When the reference meridian used is the true (geographic) meridian, the resulting horizontal angle is specifically called the true bearing of the line.

q: 35. If the sights are vertical
options: the eye vane and object vane will be in same line
the eye vane, object vane and string will be parallel and in same line
there will be no local attraction
explain: Correct vertical alignment ensures that the line of sight accurately reflects the bearing on the graduated ring.

q: 36. Which of the following instruments can be used for the direct measurement of directions?
explain: Both the surveyor's compass and the prismatic compass are magnetic instruments capable of directly measuring the bearing/direction of a line in the field.

q: 37. The needle is adjusted for
explain: To ensure accuracy, the needle must be balanced (to counter dip), sensitive (to move freely), and straight (to point correctly).

q: 38. The box of prismatic compass is made of
explain: The box of a prismatic compass is made of non-magnetic brass so that it does not interfere with or attract the freely suspended magnetic needle.

q: 39. If the end stations of a line are free from local attraction, then the difference in between fore and back bearing of that line should be
explain: In the absence of local attraction at either end station, the fore bearing and back bearing of a line always differ by exactly 180 degrees.

q: 40. The imaginary line joining the points if zero declination on the surface of the earth is called as
explain: The agonic line is the specific isogonic line that joins points having zero magnetic declination, i.e., where magnetic north coincides with true north.

q: 41. The variation in magnetic declination may be
explain: Magnetic declination is known to vary due to diurnal (daily), annual, and secular (long-term, over years) causes, so all types of variation apply.

q: 42. In the prismatic compass
options: the magnetic needle moves with the box
the line of sight doesn't move with the box
the magnetic needle and graduated circle do not move with the box
explain: In a prismatic compass, the magnetic needle (with attached graduated ring) stays fixed relative to magnetic north while the box (and line of sight/sighting vane) rotates freely; so the line of sight does not move with the fixed needle assembly.

q: 43. If the fore bearing of a line is observed to be 12 deg 24', the back bearing of line AB should be
explain: Back bearing = Fore bearing + 180 deg (since FB < 180 deg) = 12 deg 24' + 180 deg = 192 deg 24'.

q: 44. Local attraction in compass surveying may exist due to
options: incorrect leveling of the magnetic needle
loss of magnetism of the needle
friction of the needle at the pivot
presence of magnetic substances near the instrument
explain: Local attraction is caused by external magnetic disturbances - the presence of magnetic substances (iron objects, power lines, etc.) near the compass station - which deflect the needle from true magnetic north.

q: 45. The lines of force of earth's magnetic field are parallel to the earth's surface
options: at right angles to the poles
at 45 deg to the line joining poles
explain: Near the equator, the earth's magnetic field lines run roughly horizontal (parallel to the surface), which is why the dip of the needle is close to zero there; near the poles the field lines are nearly vertical.

q: 46. The horizontal angle between true meridian and magnetic meridian at a place is called
explain: This angle, between the true meridian and the magnetic meridian at a place, is by definition the magnetic declination.

q: 47. At magnetic poles, the dip of magnetic needle is
explain: At the magnetic poles, a freely suspended needle aligns itself vertically with the earth's field, giving a dip of 90 degrees.

q: 48. The least count of prismatic compass is
explain: A standard prismatic compass is generally graduated to allow readings to a least count of about 15 minutes of arc.

q: 49. The total number of zeroes graduated on a surveyor's compass is
explain: A surveyor's compass, graduated in the quadrantal bearing system, has two zero marks (at the North and South ends), unlike the prismatic compass which has only a single zero (North) on its whole-circle graduated ring.

q: 50. At the equator, the amount of dip is
explain: At the magnetic equator, the earth's magnetic field lines run horizontal, so a freely suspended needle shows zero dip.
